Here’s the Thing
           CESI, Exia 13/04/2026


                                  
Team:
The Chairperson: BENAZIZ Rayane
The Secretary: HAMOUR Ramy
The scribe: RADI Selma
The Steward: BOUYACOUB Rayan

Group 02





Glossary
Words to be defined :
Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, recruiter, etc.) 
it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).

Key Words :
CEO
Elevator
Business
Job Application
Situation.
Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.

Expected outcome:
Prepare an elevator pitch

Needs:
1. Tenses (verb tenses)
Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.
Present tense
The present is used for:
		habits (things you do regularly) 
		general facts 
Structure: subject + base verb
Example: “I work”, “I study”
With he / she / it, you add -s:
“She works”, “He studies”
Use it when something is always true or happens often.


Past tense
The past is used for finished actions.
There are two types of verbs:
Regular verbs: add -ed
Example: “work → worked”
Irregular verbs: change completely
Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”
Use it when the action is clearly in the past
Future tense
The future uses will + verb.
Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”
Use it for:
		decisions made now 
		predictions 
Present conditional
The conditional uses would + verb.
Example: “I would work if I had time”
Use it for:
		imaginary situations 
		polite requests 
Example: “I would like to apply for this job”







2. Formal English
Formal English is used in professional communication.
It is more polite, structured, and precise.
You avoid simple or casual words.
Examples:
“I want” → “I would like”
“I think” → “I believe”
“I got” → “I obtained”
“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”
You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.
Example:
Informal: “I want a job in IT”
Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”

3. Adjectives and Adverbs
Adjectives
Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).
They usually come before the noun:
Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”
They can also come after “to be”:
Example: “She is intelligent”
Adverbs
Adverbs describe a verb (an action).
They often end in -ly:
quick → quickly
slow → slowly
Example:
“She works quickly” (how does she work?)




Important difference
Adjective = describes a thing
Adverb = describes an action
“She is quick” → describes the person
“She works quickly” → describes how she works


4. Highlighting achievements
This is very important in CVs, interviews, and pitches.
You should not just say what you did, but also show the result.
Good structure:
Action + result + detail (number, impact, improvement)
Examples
Basic:
“I worked on a project”
Better:
“I successfully completed a project”
Stronger:
“I successfully completed a project that improved system performance by 20%”
Basic:
“I made a website”
Better:
“I developed a website used by 500 users”
Useful action verbs
Use strong verbs to sound professional:
		Developed 
		Managed 
		Created 
		Improved 
		Increased 
		Optimized 
		Designed

They usually come before the noun:

They can also come after “to be”:

Adverbs
Adverbs describe a verb (an action).
They often end in -ly:
quick → quickly
slow → slowly
Example:
“She works quickly” (how does she work?)




Important difference
Adjective = describes a thing
Adverb = describes an action
“She is quick” → describes the person
“She works quickly” → describes how she works

slow → slowly

                          'Glossary\n'
                          'Words to be defined :\n'
                          'Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or '
                          'product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, '
                          'recruiter, etc.) \n'
                          'it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in '
                          'a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Key Words :\n'
                          'CEO\n'
                          'Elevator\n'
                          'Business\n'
                          'Job Application\n'
                          'Situation.\n'
                          'Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Expected outcome:\n'
                          'Prepare an elevator pitch\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Needs:\n'
                          '1. Tenses (verb tenses)\n'
                          'Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.\n'
                          'Present tense\n'
                          'The present is used for:\n'
                          '\t\thabits (things you do regularly) \n'
                          '\t\tgeneral facts \n'
                          'Structure: subject + base verb\n'
                          'Example: “I work”, “I study”\n'
                          'With he / she / it, you add -s:\n'
                          '“She works”, “He studies”\n'
                          'Use it when something is always true or happens often.\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Past tense\n'
                          'The past is used for finished actions.\n'
                          'There are two types of verbs:\n'
                          'Regular verbs: add -ed\n'
                          'Example: “work → worked”\n'
                          'Irregular verbs: change completely\n'
                          'Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”\n'
                          'Use it when the action is clearly in the past\n'
                          'Future tense\n'
                          'The future uses will + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\tdecisions made now \n'
                          '\t\tpredictions \n'
                          'Present conditional\n'
                          'The conditional uses would + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I would work if I had time”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\timaginary situations \n'
                          '\t\tpolite requests \n'
                          'Example: “I would like to apply for this job”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'

                          'It is more polite, structured, and precise.\n'
                          'You avoid simple or casual words.\n'
                          'Examples:\n'
                          '“I want” → “I would like”\n'
                          '“I think” → “I believe”\n'
                          '“I got” → “I obtained”\n'
                          '“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”\n'
                          'You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          'Informal: “I want a job in IT”\n'
                          'Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”\n'
                          '\n'

                          'Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).\n'

                          'Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”\n'
                          'They can also come after “to be”:\n'
                          'Example: “She is intelligent”\n'
                          'Adverbs\n'
                          'Adverbs describe a verb (an action).\n'
                          'They often end in -ly:\n'
                          'quick → quickly\n'
                          'slow → slowly\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          '“She works quickly” (how does she work?)\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Important difference\n'
                          'Adjective = describes a thing\n'
                          'Adverb = describes an action\n'
                          '“She is quick” → describes the person\n'
                          '“She works quickly” → describes how she works\n'
                          '\n'

Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).
They usually come before the noun:
Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”
They can also come after “to be”:
Example: “She is intelligent”
Adverbs
Adverbs describe a verb (an action).
They often end in -ly:
quick → quickly
slow → slowly
Example:
“She works quickly” (how does she work?)




Important difference
Adjective = describes a thing
Adverb = describes an action
“She is quick” → describes the person
“She works quickly” → describes how she works

Adverbs

quick → quickly
slow → slowly
Example:

                          'Glossary\n'
                          'Words to be defined :\n'
                          'Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or '
                          'product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, '
                          'recruiter, etc.) \n'
                          'it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in '
                          'a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Key Words :\n'
                          'CEO\n'
                          'Elevator\n'
                          'Business\n'
                          'Job Application\n'
                          'Situation.\n'
                          'Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Expected outcome:\n'
                          'Prepare an elevator pitch\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Needs:\n'
                          '1. Tenses (verb tenses)\n'
                          'Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.\n'
                          'Present tense\n'
                          'The present is used for:\n'
                          '\t\thabits (things you do regularly) \n'
                          '\t\tgeneral facts \n'
                          'Structure: subject + base verb\n'
                          'Example: “I work”, “I study”\n'
                          'With he / she / it, you add -s:\n'
                          '“She works”, “He studies”\n'
                          'Use it when something is always true or happens often.\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Past tense\n'
                          'The past is used for finished actions.\n'
                          'There are two types of verbs:\n'
                          'Regular verbs: add -ed\n'
                          'Example: “work → worked”\n'
                          'Irregular verbs: change completely\n'
                          'Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”\n'
                          'Use it when the action is clearly in the past\n'
                          'Future tense\n'
                          'The future uses will + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\tdecisions made now \n'
                          '\t\tpredictions \n'
                          'Present conditional\n'
                          'The conditional uses would + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I would work if I had time”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\timaginary situations \n'
                          '\t\tpolite requests \n'
                          'Example: “I would like to apply for this job”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '2. Formal English\n'
                          'Formal English is used in professional communication.\n'
                          'It is more polite, structured, and precise.\n'
                          'You avoid simple or casual words.\n'
                          'Examples:\n'
                          '“I want” → “I would like”\n'
                          '“I think” → “I believe”\n'
                          '“I got” → “I obtained”\n'
                          '“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”\n'
                          'You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          'Informal: “I want a job in IT”\n'
                          'Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '3. Adjectives and Adverbs\n'
                          'Adjectives\n'
                          'Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).\n'
                          'They usually come before the noun:\n'
                          'Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”\n'
                          'They can also come after “to be”:\n'
                          'Example: “She is intelligent”\n'
                          'Adverbs\n'
                          'Adverbs describe a verb (an action).\n'
                          'They often end in -ly:\n'
                          'quick → quickly\n'
                          'slow → slowly\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          '“She works quickly” (how does she work?)\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Important difference\n'
                          'Adjective = describes a thing\n'
                          'Adverb = describes an action\n'
                          '“She is quick” → describes the person\n'
                          '“She works quickly” → describes how she works\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '4. Highlighting achievements\n'
                          'This is very important in CVs, interviews, and pitches.\n'
                          'You should not just say what you did, but also show the result.\n'
                          'Good structure:\n'
                          'Action + result + detail (number, impact, improvement)\n'
                          'Examples\n'
                          'Basic:\n'
                          '“I worked on a project”\n'
                          'Better:\n'
                          '“I successfully completed a project”\n'
                          'Stronger:\n'
                          '“I successfully completed a project that improved system performance by '
                          '20%”\n'
                          'Basic:\n'
                          '“I made a website”\n'
                          'Better:\n'
                          '“I developed a website used by 500 users”\n'
                          'Useful action verbs\n'
                          'Use strong verbs to sound professional:\n'
                          '\t\tDeveloped \n'
                          '\t\tManaged \n'
                          '\t\tCreated \n'
                          '\t\tImproved \n'
                          '\t\tIncreased \n'
                          '\t\tOptimized \n'
                          '\t\tDesigned \n'

             'page_text': '\n'
                          'Glossary\n'
                          'Words to be defined :\n'
                          'Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or '
                          'product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, '
                          'recruiter, etc.) \n'
                          'it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in '
                          'a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Key Words :\n'
                          'CEO\n'
                          'Elevator\n'
                          'Business\n'
                          'Job Application\n'
                          'Situation.\n'
                          'Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Expected outcome:\n'
                          'Prepare an elevator pitch\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Needs:\n'
                          '1. Tenses (verb tenses)\n'
                          'Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.\n'
                          'Present tense\n'
                          'The present is used for:\n'
                          '\t\thabits (things you do regularly) \n'
                          '\t\tgeneral facts \n'
                          'Structure: subject + base verb\n'
                          'Example: “I work”, “I study”\n'
                          'With he / she / it, you add -s:\n'
                          '“She works”, “He studies”\n'
                          'Use it when something is always true or happens often.\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Past tense\n'
                          'The past is used for finished actions.\n'
                          'There are two types of verbs:\n'
                          'Regular verbs: add -ed\n'
                          'Example: “work → worked”\n'
                          'Irregular verbs: change completely\n'
                          'Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”\n'
                          'Use it when the action is clearly in the past\n'
                          'Future tense\n'
                          'The future uses will + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\tdecisions made now \n'
                          '\t\tpredictions \n'
                          'Present conditional\n'
                          'The conditional uses would + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I would work if I had time”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\timaginary situations \n'
                          '\t\tpolite requests \n'
                          'Example: “I would like to apply for this job”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '2. Formal English\n'
                          'Formal English is used in professional communication.\n'
                          'It is more polite, structured, and precise.\n'
                          'You avoid simple or casual words.\n'
                          'Examples:\n'
                          '“I want” → “I would like”\n'
                          '“I think” → “I believe”\n'
                          '“I got” → “I obtained”\n'
                          '“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”\n'
                          'You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          'Informal: “I want a job in IT”\n'
                          'Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '3. Adjectives and Adverbs\n'
                          'Adjectives\n'
                          'Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).\n'
                          'They usually come before the noun:\n'
                          'Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”\n'
                          'They can also come after “to be”:\n'
                          'Example: “She is intelligent”\n'
                          'Adverbs\n'
                          'Adverbs describe a verb (an action).\n'
                          'They often end in -ly:\n'
                          'quick → quickly\n'
                          'slow → slowly\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          '“She works quickly” (how does she work?)\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Important difference\n'
                          'Adjective = describes a thing\n'
                          'Adverb = describes an action\n'
                          '“She is quick” → describes the person\n'
                          '“She works quickly” → describes how she works\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '4. Highlighting achievements\n'
                          'This is very important in CVs, interviews, and pitches.\n'
                          'You should not just say what you did, but also show the result.\n'
                          'Good structure:\n'
                          'Action + result + detail (number, impact, improvement)\n'
                          'Examples\n'
                          'Basic:\n'
                          '“I worked on a project”\n'
                          'Better:\n'
                          '“I successfully completed a project”\n'
                          'Stronger:\n'
                          '“I successfully completed a project that improved system performance by '
                          '20%”\n'
                          'Basic:\n'
                          '“I made a website”\n'
                          'Better:\n'
                          '“I developed a website used by 500 users”\n'
                          'Useful action verbs\n'
                          'Use strong verbs to sound professional:\n'
                          '\t\tDeveloped \n'
                          '\t\tManaged \n'
                          '\t\tCreated \n'
                          '\t\tImproved \n'
                          '\t\tIncreased \n'
                          '\t\tOptimized \n'
                          '\t\tDesigned \n'
                          '\n'
                          'Vocabulary:\n'

Here’s the Thing
           CESI, Exia 13/04/2026

Team:
The Chairperson: BENAZIZ Rayane
The Secretary: HAMOUR Ramy
The scribe: RADI Selma
The Steward: BOUYACOUB Rayan

Glossary
Words to be defined :
Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, recruiter, etc.) 
it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).

Key Words :
CEO
Elevator
Business
Job Application
Situation.
Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.

Expected outcome:
Prepare an elevator pitch

Needs:
1. Tenses (verb tenses)
Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.
Present tense
The present is used for:

habits (things you do regularly) 
		general facts

Structure: subject + base verb
Example: “I work”, “I study”
With he / she / it, you add -s:
“She works”, “He studies”
Use it when something is always true or happens often.

Past tense
The past is used for finished actions.
There are two types of verbs:
Regular verbs: add -ed
Example: “work → worked”
Irregular verbs: change completely
Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”
Use it when the action is clearly in the past
Future tense
The future uses will + verb.
Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”
Use it for:

decisions made now 
		predictions
Present conditional
The conditional uses would + verb.
“I would work if I had time”

imaginary situations 
		polite requests
Example: “I would like to apply for this job”

2. Formal English
Formal English is used in professional communication.
It is more polite, structured, and precise.
You avoid simple or casual words.
Examples:
“I want” → “I would like”
“I think” → “I believe”
“I got” → “I obtained”
“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”
You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.
Example:
Informal: “I want a job in IT”
Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”

3. Adjectives and Adverbs

Glossary
Words to be defined :
Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, recruiter, etc.) 
it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).

Key Words :
CEO
Elevator
Business
Job Application
Situation.
Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.

Expected outcome:
Prepare an elevator pitch

Needs:
1. Tenses (verb tenses)
Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.
Present tense
The present is used for:
		habits (things you do regularly) 
		general facts 
Structure: subject + base verb
Example: “I work”, “I study”
With he / she / it, you add -s:
“She works”, “He studies”
Use it when something is always true or happens often.


Past tense
The past is used for finished actions.
There are two types of verbs:
Regular verbs: add -ed
Example: “work → worked”
Irregular verbs: change completely
Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”
Use it when the action is clearly in the past
Future tense
The future uses will + verb.
Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”
Use it for:
		decisions made now 
		predictions 
Present conditional
The conditional uses would + verb.
Example: “I would work if I had time”
Use it for:
		imaginary situations 
		polite requests 
Example: “I would like to apply for this job”







2. Formal English
Formal English is used in professional communication.
It is more polite, structured, and precise.
You avoid simple or casual words.
Examples:
“I want” → “I would like”
“I think” → “I believe”
“I got” → “I obtained”
“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”
You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.
Example:
Informal: “I want a job in IT”
Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”

3. Adjectives and Adverbs
Adjectives
Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).
They usually come before the noun:
Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”
They can also come after “to be”:
Example: “She is intelligent”
Adverbs
Adverbs describe a verb (an action).
They often end in -ly:
quick → quickly
slow → slowly
Example:
“She works quickly” (how does she work?)




Important difference
Adjective = describes a thing
Adverb = describes an action
“She is quick” → describes the person
“She works quickly” → describes how she works


4. Highlighting achievements
This is very important in CVs, interviews, and pitches.
You should not just say what you did, but also show the result.
Good structure:
Action + result + detail (number, impact, improvement)
Examples
Basic:
“I worked on a project”
Better:
“I successfully completed a project”
Stronger:
“I successfully completed a project that improved system performance by 20%”
Basic:
“I made a website”
Better:
“I developed a website used by 500 users”
Useful action verbs
Use strong verbs to sound professional:
		Developed 
		Managed 
		Created 
		Improved 
		Increased 
		Optimized 
		Designed

                          'Glossary\n'
                          'Words to be defined :\n'
                          'Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or '
                          'product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, '
                          'recruiter, etc.) \n'
                          'it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in '
                          'a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Key Words :\n'
                          'CEO\n'
                          'Elevator\n'
                          'Business\n'
                          'Job Application\n'
                          'Situation.\n'
                          'Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Expected outcome:\n'
                          'Prepare an elevator pitch\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Needs:\n'
                          '1. Tenses (verb tenses)\n'
                          'Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.\n'
                          'Present tense\n'
                          'The present is used for:\n'
                          '\t\thabits (things you do regularly) \n'
                          '\t\tgeneral facts \n'
                          'Structure: subject + base verb\n'
                          'Example: “I work”, “I study”\n'
                          'With he / she / it, you add -s:\n'
                          '“She works”, “He studies”\n'
                          'Use it when something is always true or happens often.\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Past tense\n'
                          'The past is used for finished actions.\n'
                          'There are two types of verbs:\n'
                          'Regular verbs: add -ed\n'
                          'Example: “work → worked”\n'
                          'Irregular verbs: change completely\n'
                          'Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”\n'
                          'Use it when the action is clearly in the past\n'
                          'Future tense\n'
                          'The future uses will + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\tdecisions made now \n'
                          '\t\tpredictions \n'
                          'Present conditional\n'
                          'The conditional uses would + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I would work if I had time”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\timaginary situations \n'
                          '\t\tpolite requests \n'
                          'Example: “I would like to apply for this job”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'

                          'It is more polite, structured, and precise.\n'
                          'You avoid simple or casual words.\n'
                          'Examples:\n'
                          '“I want” → “I would like”\n'
                          '“I think” → “I believe”\n'
                          '“I got” → “I obtained”\n'
                          '“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”\n'
                          'You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          'Informal: “I want a job in IT”\n'
                          'Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”\n'
                          '\n'

                          'Adjectives\n'
                          'Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).\n'
                          'They usually come before the noun:\n'
                          'Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”\n'
                          'They can also come after “to be”:\n'
                          'Example: “She is intelligent”\n'
                          'Adverbs\n'
                          'Adverbs describe a verb (an action).\n'
                          'They often end in -ly:\n'
                          'quick → quickly\n'
                          'slow → slowly\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          '“She works quickly” (how does she work?)\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Important difference\n'
                          'Adjective = describes a thing\n'
                          'Adverb = describes an action\n'
                          '“She is quick” → describes the person\n'
                          '“She works quickly” → describes how she works\n'

                          'Words to be defined :\n'

                          'Use it when something is always true or happens often.\n'

                          'There are two types of verbs:\n'
                          'Regular verbs: add -ed\n'

                          'Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”\n'

Here’s the Thing
           CESI, Exia 13/04/2026

Team:
The Chairperson: BENAZIZ Rayane
The Secretary: HAMOUR Ramy
The scribe: RADI Selma
The Steward: BOUYACOUB Rayan
Group 02

Glossary
Words to be defined :
Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, recruiter, etc.) 
it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).

Key Words :
CEO
Elevator
Business
Job Application
Situation.
Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.

Expected outcome:
Prepare an elevator pitch

Needs:
1. Tenses (verb tenses)
Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.
Present tense
The present is used for:

habits (things you do regularly) 
		general facts

Structure: subject + base verb
Example: “I work”, “I study”
With he / she / it, you add -s:
“She works”, “He studies”
Use it when something is always true or happens often.

Past tense
The past is used for finished actions.
There are two types of verbs:
Regular verbs: add -ed
Example: “work → worked”
Irregular verbs: change completely
Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”
Use it when the action is clearly in the past
Future tense
The future uses will + verb.
Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”
Use it for:

decisions made now 
		predictions
Present conditional
The conditional uses would + verb.
Example:
“I would work if I had time”
Use it for:

imaginary situations 
		polite requests
Example: “I would like to apply for this job”

2. Formal English
Formal English is used in professional communication.
It is more polite, structured, and precise.
You avoid simple or casual words.
Examples:
“I want” → “I would like”
“I think” → “I believe”
“I got” → “I obtained”
“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”
You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.
Example:
Informal: “I want a job in IT”
Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”

3. Adjectives and Adverbs
Adjectives
Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).
They usually come before the noun:
Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”
They can also come after “to be”:
Example: “She is intelligent”
Adverbs
Adverbs describe a verb (an action).
They often end in -ly:
quick → quickly
slow → slowly
Example:
“She works quickly” (how does she work?)




Important difference
Adjective = describes a thing
Adverb = describes an action
“She is quick” → describes the person
“She works quickly” → describes how she works

4. Highlighting achievements
This is very important in CVs, interviews, and pitches.
You should not just say what you did, but also show the result.
Good structure:
Action + result + detail (number, impact, improvement)
Examples
Basic:
“I worked on a project”
Better:
“I successfully completed a project”
Stronger:
“I successfully completed a project that improved system performance by 20%”
Basic:
“I made a website”
Better:
“I developed a website used by 500 users”
Useful action verbs
Use strong verbs to sound professional:

Developed 
		Managed 
		Created 
		Improved 
		Increased 
		Optimized 
		Designed

Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).
They usually come before the noun:
Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”
They can also come after “to be”:
Example: “She is intelligent”
Adverbs
Adverbs describe a verb (an action).
They often end in -ly:
quick → quickly
slow → slowly
Example:
“She works quickly” (how does she work?)




Important difference
Adjective = describes a thing
Adverb = describes an action
“She is quick” → describes the person
“She works quickly” → describes how she works

slow → slowly

                          'Glossary\n'
                          'Words to be defined :\n'
                          'Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or '
                          'product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, '
                          'recruiter, etc.) \n'
                          'it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in '
                          'a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).\n'
                          '\n'

                          'Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Expected outcome:\n'
                          'Prepare an elevator pitch\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Needs:\n'
                          '1. Tenses (verb tenses)\n'
                          'Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.\n'
                          'Present tense\n'
                          'The present is used for:\n'
                          '\t\thabits (things you do regularly) \n'
                          '\t\tgeneral facts \n'
                          'Structure: subject + base verb\n'
                          'Example: “I work”, “I study”\n'
                          'With he / she / it, you add -s:\n'
                          '“She works”, “He studies”\n'
                          'Use it when something is always true or happens often.\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Past tense\n'
                          'The past is used for finished actions.\n'
                          'There are two types of verbs:\n'
                          'Regular verbs: add -ed\n'
                          'Example: “work → worked”\n'
                          'Irregular verbs: change completely\n'
                          'Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”\n'
                          'Use it when the action is clearly in the past\n'
                          'Future tense\n'
                          'The future uses will + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\tdecisions made now \n'
                          '\t\tpredictions \n'
                          'Present conditional\n'
                          'The conditional uses would + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I would work if I had time”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\timaginary situations \n'
                          '\t\tpolite requests \n'
                          'Example: “I would like to apply for this job”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '2. Formal English\n'
                          'Formal English is used in professional communication.\n'
                          'It is more polite, structured, and precise.\n'
                          'You avoid simple or casual words.\n'
                          'Examples:\n'
                          '“I want” → “I would like”\n'
                          '“I think” → “I believe”\n'
                          '“I got” → “I obtained”\n'
                          '“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”\n'
                          'You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          'Informal: “I want a job in IT”\n'
                          'Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '3. Adjectives and Adverbs\n'
                          'Adjectives\n'
                          'Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).\n'
                          'They usually come before the noun:\n'
                          'Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”\n'
                          'They can also come after “to be”:\n'
                          'Example: “She is intelligent”\n'
                          'Adverbs\n'
                          'Adverbs describe a verb (an action).\n'
                          'They often end in -ly:\n'
                          'quick → quickly\n'
                          'slow → slowly\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          '“She works quickly” (how does she work?)\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Important difference\n'
                          'Adjective = describes a thing\n'
                          'Adverb = describes an action\n'
                          '“She is quick” → describes the person\n'
                          '“She works quickly” → describes how she works\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '4. Highlighting achievements\n'
                          'This is very important in CVs, interviews, and pitches.\n'
                          'You should not just say what you did, but also show the result.\n'
                          'Good structure:\n'
                          'Action + result + detail (number, impact, improvement)\n'
                          'Examples\n'
                          'Basic:\n'

                          'Basic:\n'

                          'Glossary\n'
                          'Words to be defined :\n'
                          'Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or '
                          'product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, '
                          'recruiter, etc.) \n'
                          'it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in '
                          'a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Key Words :\n'
                          'CEO\n'
                          'Elevator\n'
                          'Business\n'
                          'Job Application\n'
                          'Situation.\n'
                          'Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Expected outcome:\n'
                          'Prepare an elevator pitch\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Needs:\n'
                          '1. Tenses (verb tenses)\n'
                          'Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.\n'
                          'Present tense\n'
                          'The present is used for:\n'
                          '\t\thabits (things you do regularly) \n'
                          '\t\tgeneral facts \n'
                          'Structure: subject + base verb\n'
                          'Example: “I work”, “I study”\n'
                          'With he / she / it, you add -s:\n'
                          '“She works”, “He studies”\n'
                          'Use it when something is always true or happens often.\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Past tense\n'
                          'The past is used for finished actions.\n'
                          'There are two types of verbs:\n'
                          'Regular verbs: add -ed\n'
                          'Example: “work → worked”\n'
                          'Irregular verbs: change completely\n'
                          'Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”\n'
                          'Use it when the action is clearly in the past\n'
                          'Future tense\n'
                          'The future uses will + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\tdecisions made now \n'
                          '\t\tpredictions \n'
                          'Present conditional\n'
                          'The conditional uses would + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I would work if I had time”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\timaginary situations \n'
                          '\t\tpolite requests \n'
                          'Example: “I would like to apply for this job”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'

                          'Formal English is used in professional communication.\n'
                          'It is more polite, structured, and precise.\n'
                          'You avoid simple or casual words.\n'
                          'Examples:\n'
                          '“I want” → “I would like”\n'
                          '“I think” → “I believe”\n'
                          '“I got” → “I obtained”\n'
                          '“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”\n'
                          'You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          'Informal: “I want a job in IT”\n'
                          'Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '3. Adjectives and Adverbs\n'
                          'Adjectives\n'
                          'Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).\n'
                          'They usually come before the noun:\n'
                          'Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”\n'
                          'They can also come after “to be”:\n'
                          'Example: “She is intelligent”\n'
                          'Adverbs\n'
                          'Adverbs describe a verb (an action).\n'
                          'They often end in -ly:\n'
                          'quick → quickly\n'
                          'slow → slowly\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          '“She works quickly” (how does she work?)\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Important difference\n'
                          'Adjective = describes a thing\n'
                          'Adverb = describes an action\n'
                          '“She is quick” → describes the person\n'
                          '“She works quickly” → describes how she works\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'

Here’s the Thing
           CESI, Exia 13/04/2026


                                  
Team:
The Chairperson: BENAZIZ Rayane
The Secretary: HAMOUR Ramy
The scribe: RADI Selma
The Steward: BOUYACOUB Rayan

Group 02





Glossary
Words to be defined :
Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, recruiter, etc.) 
it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).

Key Words :
CEO
Elevator
Business
Job Application
Situation.
Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.

Expected outcome:
Prepare an elevator pitch

Needs:
1. Tenses (verb tenses)
Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.
Present tense
The present is used for:
		habits (things you do regularly) 
		general facts 
Structure: subject + base verb
Example: “I work”, “I study”
With he / she / it, you add -s:
“She works”, “He studies”
Use it when something is always true or happens often.


Past tense
The past is used for finished actions.
There are two types of verbs:
Regular verbs: add -ed
Example: “work → worked”
Irregular verbs: change completely
Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”
Use it when the action is clearly in the past
Future tense
The future uses will + verb.
Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”
Use it for:
		decisions made now 
		predictions 
Present conditional
The conditional uses would + verb.
Example: “I would work if I had time”
Use it for:
		imaginary situations 
		polite requests 
Example: “I would like to apply for this job”







2. Formal English
Formal English is used in professional communication.
It is more polite, structured, and precise.
You avoid simple or casual words.
Examples:
“I want” → “I would like”
“I think” → “I believe”
“I got” → “I obtained”
“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”
You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.
Example:
Informal: “I want a job in IT”
Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”

3. Adjectives and Adverbs
Adjectives
Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).
They usually come before the noun:
Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”
They can also come after “to be”:
Example: “She is intelligent”
Adverbs
Adverbs describe a verb (an action).
They often end in -ly:
quick → quickly
slow → slowly
Example:
“She works quickly” (how does she work?)




Important difference
Adjective = describes a thing
Adverb = describes an action
“She is quick” → describes the person
“She works quickly” → describes how she works


4. Highlighting achievements
This is very important in CVs, interviews, and pitches.
You should not just say what you did, but also show the result.
Good structure:
Action + result + detail (number, impact, improvement)
Examples
Basic:
“I worked on a project”
Better:
“I successfully completed a project”
Stronger:
“I successfully completed a project that improved system performance by 20%”
Basic:
“I made a website”
Better:
“I developed a website used by 500 users”
Useful action verbs
Use strong verbs to sound professional:
		Developed 
		Managed 
		Created 
		Improved 
		Increased 
		Optimized 
		Designed

3. Adjectives and Adverbs
Adjectives
Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).
They usually come before the noun:
Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”
They can also come after “to be”:
Example: “She is intelligent”
Adverbs
Adverbs describe a verb (an action).
They often end in -ly:
quick → quickly
slow → slowly
Example:
“She works quickly” (how does she work?)




Important difference
Adjective = describes a thing
Adverb = describes an action
“She is quick” → describes the person
“She works quickly” → describes how she works

                          'Present tense\n'
                          'The present is used for:\n'
                          '\t\thabits (things you do regularly) \n'
                          '\t\tgeneral facts \n'

                          'Example: “I work”, “I study”\n'

                          '“She works”, “He studies”\n'
                          'Use it when something is always true or happens often.\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Past tense\n'
                          'The past is used for finished actions.\n'
                          'There are two types of verbs:\n'
                          'Regular verbs: add -ed\n'
                          'Example: “work → worked”\n'
                          'Irregular verbs: change completely\n'
                          'Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”\n'
                          'Use it when the action is clearly in the past\n'
                          'Future tense\n'
                          'The future uses will + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\tdecisions made now \n'

                          'Use it for:\n'

                                   'text': '2. Formal English\n'
                                           'Formal English is used in professional communication.\n'
                                           'It is more polite, structured, and precise.\n'
                                           'You avoid simple or casual words.\n'
                                           'Examples:\n'
                                           '“I want” → “I would like”\n'
                                           '“I think” → “I believe”\n'
                                           '“I got” → “I obtained”\n'
                                           '“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”\n'
                                           'You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.\n'
                                           'Example:\n'
                                           'Informal: “I want a job in IT”\n'
                                           'Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”\n'
                                           '\n'},

                                   'text': '3. Adjectives and Adverbs\n'
                                           'Adjectives\n'
                                           'Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).\n'
                                           'They usually come before the noun:\n'
                                           'Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”\n'
                                           'They can also come after “to be”:\n'
                                           'Example: “She is intelligent”\n'
                                           'Adverbs\n'
                                           'Adverbs describe a verb (an action).\n'
                                           'They often end in -ly:\n'
                                           'quick → quickly\n'
                                           'slow → slowly\n'
                                           'Example:\n'
                                           '“She works quickly” (how does she work?)\n'
                                           '\n'
                                           '\n'
                                           '\n'
                                           '\n'
                                           'Important difference\n'
                                           'Adjective = describes a thing\n'
                                           'Adverb = describes an action\n'
                                           '“She is quick” → describes the person\n'
                                           '“She works quickly” → describes how she works\n'
                                           '\n'

             'page_text': '\n'
                          'Glossary\n'
                          'Words to be defined :\n'
                          'Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or '
                          'product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, '
                          'recruiter, etc.) \n'
                          'it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in '
                          'a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Key Words :\n'
                          'CEO\n'
                          'Elevator\n'
                          'Business\n'
                          'Job Application\n'
                          'Situation.\n'
                          'Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Expected outcome:\n'
                          'Prepare an elevator pitch\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Needs:\n'
                          '1. Tenses (verb tenses)\n'
                          'Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.\n'
                          'Present tense\n'
                          'The present is used for:\n'
                          '\t\thabits (things you do regularly) \n'
                          '\t\tgeneral facts \n'
                          'Structure: subject + base verb\n'
                          'Example: “I work”, “I study”\n'
                          'With he / she / it, you add -s:\n'
                          '“She works”, “He studies”\n'
                          'Use it when something is always true or happens often.\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Past tense\n'
                          'The past is used for finished actions.\n'
                          'There are two types of verbs:\n'
                          'Regular verbs: add -ed\n'
                          'Example: “work → worked”\n'
                          'Irregular verbs: change completely\n'
                          'Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”\n'
                          'Use it when the action is clearly in the past\n'
                          'Future tense\n'
                          'The future uses will + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\tdecisions made now \n'
                          '\t\tpredictions \n'
                          'Present conditional\n'
                          'The conditional uses would + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I would work if I had time”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\timaginary situations \n'
                          '\t\tpolite requests \n'
                          'Example: “I would like to apply for this job”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '2. Formal English\n'
                          'Formal English is used in professional communication.\n'
                          'It is more polite, structured, and precise.\n'
                          'You avoid simple or casual words.\n'
                          'Examples:\n'
                          '“I want” → “I would like”\n'
                          '“I think” → “I believe”\n'
                          '“I got” → “I obtained”\n'
                          '“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”\n'
                          'You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          'Informal: “I want a job in IT”\n'
                          'Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '3. Adjectives and Adverbs\n'
                          'Adjectives\n'
                          'Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).\n'
                          'They usually come before the noun:\n'
                          'Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”\n'
                          'They can also come after “to be”:\n'
                          'Example: “She is intelligent”\n'
                          'Adverbs\n'
                          'Adverbs describe a verb (an action).\n'
                          'They often end in -ly:\n'
                          'quick → quickly\n'
                          'slow → slowly\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          '“She works quickly” (how does she work?)\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Important difference\n'
                          'Adjective = describes a thing\n'
                          'Adverb = describes an action\n'
                          '“She is quick” → describes the person\n'
                          '“She works quickly” → describes how she works\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '4. Highlighting achievements\n'
                          'This is very important in CVs, interviews, and pitches.\n'
                          'You should not just say what you did, but also show the result.\n'
                          'Good structure:\n'
                          'Action + result + detail (number, impact, improvement)\n'
                          'Examples\n'
                          'Basic:\n'
                          '“I worked on a project”\n'
                          'Better:\n'
                          '“I successfully completed a project”\n'
                          'Stronger:\n'
                          '“I successfully completed a project that improved system performance by '
                          '20%”\n'
                          'Basic:\n'
                          '“I made a website”\n'
                          'Better:\n'
                          '“I developed a website used by 500 users”\n'
                          'Useful action verbs\n'
                          'Use strong verbs to sound professional:\n'
                          '\t\tDeveloped \n'
                          '\t\tManaged \n'
                          '\t\tCreated \n'
                          '\t\tImproved \n'
                          '\t\tIncreased \n'
                          '\t\tOptimized \n'
                          '\t\tDesigned \n'
                          '\n'
                          'Vocabulary:\n'

INPUT: 3. Adjectives and Adverbs
Adjectives
Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).
They usually come before the noun:
Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”
They can also come after “to be”:
Example: “She is intelligent”
Adverbs
Adverbs describe a verb (an action).
They often end in -ly:
quick → quickly
slow → slowly
Example:
“She works quickly” (how does she work?)




Important difference
Adjective = describes a thing
Adverb = describes an action
“She is quick” → describes the person
“She works quickly” → describes how she works

Adverbs

slow → slowly

                          'Glossary\n'
                          'Words to be defined :\n'
                          'Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or '
                          'product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, '
                          'recruiter, etc.) \n'
                          'it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in '
                          'a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Key Words :\n'
                          'CEO\n'
                          'Elevator\n'
                          'Business\n'
                          'Job Application\n'
                          'Situation.\n'
                          'Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Expected outcome:\n'
                          'Prepare an elevator pitch\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Needs:\n'
                          '1. Tenses (verb tenses)\n'
                          'Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.\n'
                          'Present tense\n'
                          'The present is used for:\n'
                          '\t\thabits (things you do regularly) \n'
                          '\t\tgeneral facts \n'
                          'Structure: subject + base verb\n'
                          'Example: “I work”, “I study”\n'
                          'With he / she / it, you add -s:\n'
                          '“She works”, “He studies”\n'
                          'Use it when something is always true or happens often.\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Past tense\n'
                          'The past is used for finished actions.\n'
                          'There are two types of verbs:\n'
                          'Regular verbs: add -ed\n'
                          'Example: “work → worked”\n'
                          'Irregular verbs: change completely\n'
                          'Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”\n'
                          'Use it when the action is clearly in the past\n'
                          'Future tense\n'
                          'The future uses will + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\tdecisions made now \n'
                          '\t\tpredictions \n'
                          'Present conditional\n'
                          'The conditional uses would + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I would work if I had time”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\timaginary situations \n'
                          '\t\tpolite requests \n'
                          'Example: “I would like to apply for this job”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'

                          'It is more polite, structured, and precise.\n'
                          'You avoid simple or casual words.\n'
                          'Examples:\n'
                          '“I want” → “I would like”\n'
                          '“I think” → “I believe”\n'
                          '“I got” → “I obtained”\n'
                          '“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”\n'
                          'You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          'Informal: “I want a job in IT”\n'
                          'Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '3. Adjectives and Adverbs\n'
                          'Adjectives\n'
                          'Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).\n'
                          'They usually come before the noun:\n'
                          'Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”\n'
                          'They can also come after “to be”:\n'
                          'Example: “She is intelligent”\n'
                          'Adverbs\n'
                          'Adverbs describe a verb (an action).\n'
                          'They often end in -ly:\n'
                          'quick → quickly\n'
                          'slow → slowly\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          '“She works quickly” (how does she work?)\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Important difference\n'
                          'Adjective = describes a thing\n'
                          'Adverb = describes an action\n'
                          '“She is quick” → describes the person\n'
                          '“She works quickly” → describes how she works\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'

INPUT: 3. Adjectives and Adverbs
Adjectives
Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).
They usually come before the noun:
Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”
They can also come after “to be”:
Example: “She is intelligent”
Adverbs
Adverbs describe a verb (an action).
They often end in -ly:
quick → quickly
slow → slowly
Example:
“She works quickly” (how does she work?)




Important difference
Adjective = describes a thing
Adverb = describes an action
“She is quick” → describes the person
“She works quickly” → describes how she works

Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).
They usually come before the noun:
Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”
They can also come after “to be”:
Example: “She is intelligent”
Adverbs
Adverbs describe a verb (an action).
They often end in -ly:
quick → quickly
slow → slowly
Example:
“She works quickly” (how does she work?)




Important difference
Adjective = describes a thing
Adverb = describes an action
“She is quick” → describes the person
“She works quickly” → describes how she works

                          '2. Formal English\n'
                          'Formal English is used in professional communication.\n'
                          'It is more polite, structured, and precise.\n'
                          'You avoid simple or casual words.\n'
                          'Examples:\n'
                          '“I want” → “I would like”\n'
                          '“I think” → “I believe”\n'
                          '“I got” → “I obtained”\n'
                          '“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”\n'
                          'You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          'Informal: “I want a job in IT”\n'
                          'Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '3. Adjectives and Adverbs\n'
                          'Adjectives\n'
                          'Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).\n'
                          'They usually come before the noun:\n'
                          'Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”\n'
                          'They can also come after “to be”:\n'
                          'Example: “She is intelligent”\n'
                          'Adverbs\n'
                          'Adverbs describe a verb (an action).\n'
                          'They often end in -ly:\n'
                          'quick → quickly\n'
                          'slow → slowly\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          '“She works quickly” (how does she work?)\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Important difference\n'
                          'Adjective = describes a thing\n'
                          'Adverb = describes an action\n'
                          '“She is quick” → describes the person\n'
                          '“She works quickly” → describes how she works\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '4. Highlighting achievements\n'
                          'This is very important in CVs, interviews, and pitches.\n'
                          'You should not just say what you did, but also show the result.\n'
                          'Good structure:\n'

                          'Examples\n'
                          'Basic:\n'
                          '“I worked on a project”\n'

                          '“I successfully completed a project”\n'

                          'Glossary\n'
                          'Words to be defined :\n'
                          'Pitch : a short and impactful presentation of an idea, project, or '
                          'product, designed to quickly convince someone (a client, investor, '
                          'recruiter, etc.) \n'
                          'it’s a way to explain who you are, what you do, and why it matters… in '
                          'a very short time (usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes).\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Key Words :\n'
                          'CEO\n'
                          'Elevator\n'
                          'Business\n'
                          'Job Application\n'
                          'Situation.\n'
                          'Cillian has failed his elevator pitch, he has to improve it.\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Expected outcome:\n'
                          'Prepare an elevator pitch\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Needs:\n'
                          '1. Tenses (verb tenses)\n'
                          'Tenses tell you when an action happens: now, before, or later.\n'
                          'Present tense\n'
                          'The present is used for:\n'
                          '\t\thabits (things you do regularly) \n'
                          '\t\tgeneral facts \n'
                          'Structure: subject + base verb\n'
                          'Example: “I work”, “I study”\n'
                          'With he / she / it, you add -s:\n'
                          '“She works”, “He studies”\n'
                          'Use it when something is always true or happens often.\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Past tense\n'
                          'The past is used for finished actions.\n'
                          'There are two types of verbs:\n'
                          'Regular verbs: add -ed\n'
                          'Example: “work → worked”\n'
                          'Irregular verbs: change completely\n'
                          'Example: “go → went”, “eat → ate”\n'
                          'Use it when the action is clearly in the past\n'
                          'Future tense\n'
                          'The future uses will + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I will work”, “I will learn English”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\tdecisions made now \n'
                          '\t\tpredictions \n'
                          'Present conditional\n'
                          'The conditional uses would + verb.\n'
                          'Example: “I would work if I had time”\n'
                          'Use it for:\n'
                          '\t\timaginary situations \n'
                          '\t\tpolite requests \n'
                          'Example: “I would like to apply for this job”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '2. Formal English\n'
                          'Formal English is used in professional communication.\n'
                          'It is more polite, structured, and precise.\n'
                          'You avoid simple or casual words.\n'
                          'Examples:\n'
                          '“I want” → “I would like”\n'
                          '“I think” → “I believe”\n'
                          '“I got” → “I obtained”\n'
                          '“A lot” → “Many” or “Numerous”\n'
                          'You also use complete sentences and avoid slang.\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          'Informal: “I want a job in IT”\n'
                          'Formal: “I would like to apply for a position in IT”\n'
                          '\n'
                          '3. Adjectives and Adverbs\n'
                          'Adjectives\n'
                          'Adjectives describe a noun (person, thing, place).\n'
                          'They usually come before the noun:\n'
                          'Example: “a good student”, “a fast computer”\n'
                          'They can also come after “to be”:\n'
                          'Example: “She is intelligent”\n'
                          'Adverbs\n'
                          'Adverbs describe a verb (an action).\n'
                          'They often end in -ly:\n'
                          'quick → quickly\n'
                          'slow → slowly\n'
                          'Example:\n'
                          '“She works quickly” (how does she work?)\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          'Important difference\n'
                          'Adjective = describes a thing\n'
                          'Adverb = describes an action\n'
                          '“She is quick” → describes the person\n'
                          '“She works quickly” → describes how she works\n'
                          '\n'
                          '\n'
                          '4. Highlighting achievements\n'
                          'This is very important in CVs, interviews, and pitches.\n'
                          'You should not just say what you did, but also show the result.\n'
                          'Good structure:\n'
                          'Action + result + detail (number, impact, improvement)\n'
                          'Examples\n'
                          'Basic:\n'
                          '“I worked on a project”\n'
                          'Better:\n'
                          '“I successfully completed a project”\n'
                          'Stronger:\n'
                          '“I successfully completed a project that improved system performance by '
                          '20%”\n'
                          'Basic:\n'
                          '“I made a website”\n'
                          'Better:\n'
                          '“I developed a website used by 500 users”\n'
                          'Useful action verbs\n'
                          'Use strong verbs to sound professional:\n'
                          '\t\tDeveloped \n'
                          '\t\tManaged \n'
                          '\t\tCreated \n'
                          '\t\tImproved \n'
                          '\t\tIncreased \n'
                          '\t\tOptimized \n'
                          '\t\tDesigned \n'
                          '\n'
                          'Vocabulary:\n'
